direction.promise: An eating education taken in the order the city itself takes it: the day starts at everyday street level with the coffee-and-bread habit, moves to a market where the raw material gets explained, climbs to the one regional dish Lima is genuinely famous for at lunch, and finishes at a kitchen doing something ambitious with those same ingredients — so by bedtime the reader can taste the connection between the market stall and the tasting plate, and has the vocabulary to order confidently anywhere else in the country.
direction.trip_role: Day one is the trip's culinary education day, teaching the food vocabulary and ingredient knowledge in a low-effort, appetite-paced sequence, so that day two's adventure-focused meals can be eaten quickly and without explanation.
anchors: The signature lunch is the anchor stop
Destination dinner is the second peak, not the point

geography.required_area: Miraflores for the morning through lunch; Barranco for the afternoon walk through the evening.
geography.starting_point: Breakfast / iconic coffee stop in Miraflores.
geography.progression: Miraflores holds breakfast, the market, and the signature lunch, each within about fifteen minutes on foot of the stop before it, reading as one continuous errand. A single ride of at most twenty minutes (taxi allowed) carries the day from Miraflores to Barranco after lunch. From the afternoon walk onward, everything — the walk, the tasting, dinner, and the optional dessert/drinks — stays in Barranco on foot, within a few blocks of each other.
geography.transfer_tolerance: Exactly one transfer for the whole day, happening after lunch, at most twenty minutes door-to-door, and it is allowed to be a taxi rather than a walk.
avoid_today: Any third neighborhood beyond Miraflores and Barranco
Any crossing back to Miraflores before bed
Any stop that forces a return trip to reach the next one

rhythm.effort: Low-effort and appetite-paced, deliberately unstrenuous so it leaves enough in the tank for day two's active start.
rhythm.meal_balance: Two real meals (lunch and dinner) and two deliberately small tastes (the market's at-most-one-standing-item, and the afternoon tasting), so the reader arrives at dinner hungry rather than full.
rhythm.rest_policy: The afternoon neighborhood walk in Barranco is the day's rest and breathing space, providing digestion and a change of register between the signature lunch and the destination dinner.
rhythm.optionality: The evening dessert/drinks stop is the only optional stop and must remain genuinely droppable without the day feeling unfinished.

constraints: Scope is city-only, Lima, Peru; no venue names, opening hours, distances or prices may appear in this agreement.
Timing is evergreen — no weekday is assumed; the market choice must operate every day.
Dietary needs are unspecified — never assume 'none'.
Access needs are unspecified — never assume 'none'.
Morning through lunch stays in Miraflores, walkable, no leg more than about fifteen minutes on foot from the prior stop.
Exactly one transfer for the whole day, after lunch, Miraflores to Barranco, at most twenty minutes, taxi allowed.
Everything from the afternoon walk onward stays in Barranco on foot, within a few blocks of each other.
No third neighborhood and no crossing back to Miraflores before bed.
No stop may require a return trip to reach the next one.
The market and the afternoon tasting must never become a full meal.
Market stop: browsing and learning ingredients, at most one thing eaten standing up.
Signature lunch: one regional specialty done properly with real time at the table, not a fast in-and-out.
Afternoon tasting: one small portion, roughly twenty to thirty minutes, no table service.
Lunch and dinner venues must each do the regional specialty properly and also offer a cooked, non-seafood dish substantial enough to read as the main event.
Lunch and dinner venues must be reachable and seatable without stairs, with a bathroom on the same level.
The evening dessert/drinks stop must remain genuinely optional — droppable without the day feeling unfinished.
The day overall must stay low-effort and appetite-paced so day two's active opener is not undermined.
Day two should not repeat a market, a tasting, or a culinary-destination dinner.
Nothing is booked or paid for until the reader has filled the dietary and access blanks; research returns a shortlist with questions attached, not a locked day.

agreement_trace.decision: Which single stop is this day built around — the one that, if it fell through, would mean the day failed rather than just changed: the signature lunch, or the destination dinner?
agreement_trace.recommendation: The signature lunch is the anchor; the destination dinner is the second peak, not the point. The regional dish at midday is the thing the whole morning has been building an appetite and a vocabulary for — the market stop exists to explain what is about to arrive on that plate, and the afternoon walk exists to recover from it. Lunch is also the version of this day that cannot break: it is the meal Lima serves at the hour Lima serves it, it does not depend on a booking made weeks out, and it does not carry the price or the fixed-menu risk that makes an ambitious dinner the most fragile stop on the list. So research treats lunch as fixed — the one specialty, done properly, with real time at the table rather than a fast in-and-out — and treats dinner as the ambitious finish that should be excellent but is allowed to be swapped for a different kitchen without the day losing its spine. If only one of the two can be booked well, book lunch.
